source_capture_policy.timestamp_anchor: Rendered public-web retrieval time only; no independent external timestamp anchor.
source_capture_policy.admission_rule: Keep this relationship-graph artifact outside the prediction feature store until byte-complete source captures, SHA-256 receipts, publication vintages and independent timestamp evidence are stored.

claims_supported: BNY states that Circle USDC became the first stablecoin on BNY Digital Asset Custody, with eligible BNY clients able to store, transfer, mint and burn USDC through the institutional platform.
BNY states that it expanded its role as primary custodian of USDC reserves.
The announcement describes a BNY-mediated workflow in which clients can instruct Circle to mint USDC against dollars or redeem USDC for dollars.
limitations: The release does not disclose USDC reserve balances specifically held at BNY, BNY client counts, or actual mint/burn transaction volumes.
The announcement does not establish USDC issuance on XRPL or use of XRP as a bridge asset.
BNY and Circle copies of the joint announcement are one transaction disclosure, not independent third-party measurements.

claims_supported: Circle's own pressroom confirms BNY's expanded USDC custody, transfer, mint and burn capabilities for institutional clients.
Circle confirms BNY's primary-custodian role for USDC reserves.
limitations: This is the same joint announcement as BNY's copy and must not be counted as independent corroboration.
No BNY-specific USDC balance or transaction-level mint/burn volume is disclosed.

claims_supported: Circle's USDC page states that the portfolio of the Circle Reserve Fund, which may contain short-dated U.S. Treasuries, overnight U.S. Treasury repurchase agreements and cash, is custodied at BNY and managed by BlackRock.
Circle states that USDC is issued by regulated Circle affiliates and backed by U.S.-dollar-denominated reserve assets.
limitations: The page's BNY statement concerns the Circle Reserve Fund portfolio; it does not quantify the amount held at BNY or imply that every USDC reserve asset is held there.
The stated page data-as-of date is August 6, 2026; it is not a November 5 balance snapshot.
This is Circle issuer disclosure, not an independent custody audit.

claims_supported: Ripple states that it selected BNY as primary reserve custodian for RLUSD.
Ripple states that it would also use BNY transaction-banking services to support its operations.
limitations: The announcement does not quantify RLUSD reserve assets held at BNY or BNY's XRP holdings.
The reserve-custody appointment is not evidence that BNY purchased XRP or accepted XRP collateral.
BNY and Ripple copies of the same appointment announcement are not independent third-party measurements.

claims_supported: BNY states that its Digital Asset Custody platform now supports native XRP and RLUSD for eligible institutional clients.
BNY states that it remains primary reserve custodian for RLUSD.
BNY and Ripple describe intended future RLUSD mint/redeem through BNY, subject to final BNY and regulatory approvals.
BNY, Ripple and C2FO describe exploring tokenized trade finance on XRPL, subject to client requirements.
limitations: No XRP-specific or RLUSD-specific assets under custody, client counts, new XRP purchases or XRP collateral balances are disclosed.
Direct RLUSD mint/redeem through BNY is a future plan, not a verified live capability.
The C2FO trade-finance work is exploratory; funded receivables, capital-provider identities and production settlement volumes are not disclosed.

claims_supported: Ripple's current RLUSD product page states that RLUSD reserves are held in segregated accounts at depository institutions and securities custodians.
Ripple's page identifies BNY as the primary custodian selected for RLUSD reserves in July 2025.
Ripple describes RLUSD as issued on XRPL, Ethereum and additional supported networks.
limitations: This is issuer disclosure and does not quantify the portion of RLUSD reserves held at BNY.
The page does not establish XRP bridge use or XRP collateral balances.

relationships.interpretation: Circle and Ripple have separate stablecoin and custody relationships with BNY. The shared service provider is an indirect network connection only; these sources do not establish a direct Circle-Ripple agreement, joint venture, cross-issuance or shared reserve pool.

actual_capital_classification.rlusd_direct_mint_redeem_through_bny: future plan subject to final BNY and regulatory approvals
actual_capital_classification.classification_rule: Custody appointments, reserve-custody roles, mint/burn capabilities and exploratory tokenized-finance plans are not capital investment in XRP. Count actual cash or asset deployment only when a dated, quantified primary record or independently verified transaction establishes it.

independence_assessment.note: Multiple issuer/custodian pages improve claim traceability but do not create independent measurement of asset balances or transaction volumes.

competing_hypotheses.claim: BNY's separate USDC, RLUSD and XRP custody capabilities may lower institutional operational friction for holding and servicing multiple digital assets.
support: BNY reports institutional USDC custody/mint/burn capabilities.
BNY reports XRP and RLUSD custody support for eligible clients.
disconfirming_or_missing: No asset-specific AUC, client count, incremental account openings or net XRP purchases are disclosed.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Institutional USDC or RLUSD settlement may substitute for XRP as a bridge asset in some workflows even while XRPL activity grows.
support: C2FO's announced XRPL settlement asset is RLUSD, not XRP.
BNY's USDC mint/burn workflow is described as a fiat-to-stablecoin service, not an XRP bridge.
disconfirming_or_missing: No production C2FO settlement volumes or corridor-level asset routing are disclosed.
No evidence establishes the share of institutional flows using XRP versus stablecoins.

competing_hypotheses.claim: BNY's XRP custody capability can support existing institutional holdings without causing new purchases.
support: BNY reports safekeeping/holding/transfer capability for eligible clients.
disconfirming_or_missing: No XRP-specific AUC or net client inflow data are disclosed.

competing_hypotheses.claim: The observed Circle-Ripple network connection is BNY's role as a shared service provider, not a direct commercial partnership between the issuers.
support: The reviewed Circle and Ripple announcements describe separate issuer-to-BNY relationships.
disconfirming_or_missing: A separate direct Circle-Ripple contract or joint announcement was not established in this source set.

disconfirming_evidence: BNY-wide AUC/AUA is not XRP-specific assets under custody.
No BNY-specific USDC or RLUSD reserve balance is quantified.
No XRP purchase by BNY or BNY client is established by these custody announcements.
No XRP collateral acceptance or posted balance is disclosed.
Circle's USDC custody/mint/burn relationship with BNY does not establish USDC issuance on XRPL.
Ripple's direct RLUSD mint/redeem through BNY is described as a future plan subject to final approvals.
The Circle-Ripple connection in this artifact is an indirect shared-provider edge only; no direct agreement is established.
BNY/Ripple/C2FO tokenized trade-finance activity is exploratory and has no disclosed production funded amount or volume.
next_actions: Seek BNY asset-specific XRP, RLUSD and USDC custody balances with as-of dates and independent attestation.
Verify actual USDC mint/burn volumes through BNY separately from announced platform capability.
Track RLUSD mint/redeem through BNY only after a primary operational launch notice and transaction evidence.
Verify whether any direct Circle-Ripple agreement exists independently of the shared BNY provider relationship.
Identify C2FO participating capital providers and actual funded invoice volumes; keep historical Early Pay volumes separate.
Capture byte-complete source responses, SHA-256 receipts, publication vintages and independent timestamps before model admission.
Keep XRP spot demand, XRPL activity, USDC/RLUSD supply and custody capability as separate variables.

forecast.reason: Institutional custody capability and shared-service-provider relationships do not establish incremental XRP demand or a validated directional signal.
